title: Raw operations routes and POST /context/assess ignore the authority claim: any context:read token reads any device
description: broker_engine/main.py:188-269. /context/metric, /context/metric-history, /context/interfaces-nonzero and /context/neighbours check only need(SCOPE_READ); POST /context/assess checks only need(SCOPE_ASSESS). None calls need_authority_claims() or checks the device against authority.entities, so a token limited to entities=[Router-B] can read Router-A telemetry and topology, and assess any intent, through these routes, while POST /context/request refuses the same question with 'outside authority scope: entity'. Carry-over named in the v1.0 audit and ROADMAP 'Next' (.planning only, so it had no bead). Fix: add need_authority_claims() and an entity check (authority.covers_entity(device)) to each raw route, a purpose for them (or document that they map to one), and the placement check for assess (every placed device covered, as context_request does with D-26), all before any upstream call; tests for each route.
acceptance_criteria: Each raw route and /context/assess answers 403 'authority claims required' without the claim and 403 'outside authority scope: entity' for an uncovered device, before any Fuseki, VictoriaMetrics or TMF921 call.

title: Two loader tests read the real ontologies/abox and fail once an operator binding file exists

title: GET /context/situation answers 500 for a stored row that no longer validates (breaks the image-rollback policy)
description: broker_engine/context_request.py:620 calls StoredSituation.model_validate_json(row.body) with no handler; StoredSituation is extra='forbid' (data_contracts/situation_record.py:48). The state-file policy is additive (user_version stays 1) and 'rollback is an image rollback', but a row written by a newer image with an added field fails validation in the older image and the route returns an unhandled 500. Fix: catch pydantic.ValidationError on read, log one fixed line (no body, no id), and answer the same 404 'situation not found' (or a fixed 503); decide whether reads should ignore unknown fields instead. Add a test with a stored row carrying an extra field.

title: Knowledge retrieval holds the service lock across embedding and the Qdrant search, so knowledge requests run one at a time
description: okf_retrieval/service.py retrieve() takes self._lock for the whole of _retrieve: _ready_index (which can rebuild the collection), index.search (the embedding inference and the Qdrant query) and the applicability pass. Every request with the knowledge class is serialised behind it, and a rebuild after a file change blocks them all. Fix: hold the lock only to read or swap the shared state (files, embedder, client, collection name) and run the search outside it, or guard the rebuild separately; keep 'never raises' and the unavailable gap. Measure before and after with parallel knowledge requests.

Only their own tests import them. They are copied into the API image (COPY . .). Compose still sets BROKER_DECISION_RECORDS_PATH for the API and CLAUDE.md describes decision records as a live file, though nothing in the API opens one. An action executor in the broker's tree sits against 'the broker never decides or acts'. Decide per package: move to a separate future-layer repo or folder kept out of the image, or delete; then align CLAUDE.md, README (the 'NotWired' box) and compose.

title: bind_intent in the API container: default endpoint is localhost and the abox directory is not writable
description: Running 'docker exec contextbroker-api python -m ingestion.bind_intent' (found 2026-11-13 while binding intent 6be19f64-7cb7-4f0b-b76e-d88cf814a4c8): (1) the default --endpoint is localhost:3030 so it fails with 'the network graph did not confirm the change' until --endpoint http://fuseki:3030/network-dataset/data is passed; (2) with the endpoint the graph update is applied but /app/ontologies/abox is root-owned and the API runs as uid 10001, so 'the change was applied to the network graph but the binding file could not be written' and the ABox file for the binding does not exist. Re-running reports nothing changed, so the file cannot be regenerated. Fix: take the endpoint from FUSEKI_DATA_ENDPOINT set in compose, and either a writable abox mount or document running bind_intent from the host.
notes: Seen again 2026-11-13 binding access intent 784b3ae0 from the API container: graph applied, ABox file not written.
close_reason: bind_intent refuses before the update when the abox directory is not writable; compose sets FUSEKI_DATA_ENDPOINT for the API; README says to run it on the host. Test added.

Noted in 02-04 and in design/bitemporal-fluents.md known limits.

description: Found in Phase 1 plan 01-09 Task 1 (.planning/phases/01-protected-and-honest-baseline/01-09-PLAN.md). contextbroker-api (project contextbroker) starts on contextbroker_default only; tmf921-server lives on contextbroker-arch_default, so /health reports tmf921 not answering (503) until 'docker network connect contextbroker-arch_default contextbroker-api' is run by hand (lost on recreate). Fix options: join the external network in docker-compose.yml, or run tmf921-server from this compose file (profile tmf921).

title: Joiner reads a value and its sample time in two VictoriaMetrics queries, so a sample landing between them pairs one sample's value with the next one's time
description: broker_engine/tsdb_joiner.py:66-82 and _oldest_sample_time (:113). The value query (aggregate_over_time) and the time query (min(tlast_over_time)) are separate HTTP calls, each evaluated at VictoriaMetrics' own current time when as_of is not given. A sample written between them gives the value of sample N with the time of sample N+1. On the push path the high-water mark then records that pair, and the next assess with the real N+1 value at the same time is refused 'observation not newer than last pushed'. Fix: send both queries with the same explicit time parameter (the broker's now), or read both in one query.

title: Requirement wording says push 'older than or equal' is refused; code allows equal time with equal value

title: TMF921 assess reason says "intent server unavailable" when the intent does not exist on the server
description: Found live in Phase 3 plan 03-09: POST /context/request (assurance, current instant) for an intent id that the TMF921 server answers 404 for gives verdict inconclusive with the single reason 'intent server unavailable' (intent_management/tmf921_source.py, get_intent except Exception branch). The server is up; the intent is missing. The verdict is correct (inconclusive), only the fixed reason string misleads. Related: contextbroker-tey.11 (stale bindings for intents that no longer exist). Needs a distinct fixed string for a missing intent; keep 'never echo server text'.
